Messages.Author: Ke.
Messages.Body:
Hello all,

Am please to announce the release of Amaranth 2.0:  amaranth.vtes.co.nz

New versions of the Apps (iOS & Android) are also working there way through the App stores and should be available soon:

iOS App
Android App

Probably the most important feature of the release is deck sharing. This enables things like the starter / quick start decks (which you can also submit). It also lays the ground work for deck collaboration which may be a future feature depending on demand.

Release 2.0

Major features:  * Deck Sharing
* Happy Families
* Deck validation
* Quickstart decks
* Persistent sorting
* Play testing support
* Import from JOL
* Added Anthology Set

Changes:  Added Quickstart deck submission
Added import from JOL
Added /api/cards request
Added support for user settings
Added support for user profile
Added support for author
Added automated link URLS for: VEKN, VTES One, Secret Library, TWA, Amaranth (only accepted links)
Added /#card/100 route
Added comments for decks (mainly for Quickstart decks)
Added "banned" warning to crypt and library cards
Added "use old cards" setting
Added share button (link, facebook, twitter, email, google)
Added icons to buttons
Added decks sorting
Added decks searching
Added sort by oldest & youngest
Added Library total to text export
Added Quickstart decks
Added dice
Added happy families
Added logged in check when exporting
Added read-only deck mode
Added handle removed cards gracefully
Fixed edit deck title, desc behaviour
Fixed issue with comment modal
Fixed issue with discipline icons not changing
Fixed issues with mis-matched disciplines
Fixed select menus not closing when discipline menu opened (Crypt & Library)
App: Fixed redraw button
App: Reworked download function to exporting deck
App: Increased session time to 1 year

Messages.Author: TwoRazorReign
Messages.Body:
> Kraus wrote:
> Also, is "Horde" in there a typo? I never understood the flavor of it - should it say "Hoard" instead?
>
That's not a typo, but you bring up a very interesting point. Horde is an anthropological term meaning a small social group akin to a tribe. A hoard is a secret fund.

I see your point because (1) I'm not sure how a "Secret Horde" can be an investment, and (2) the art sure seems to indicate a secret stash like a hoard.

Here's what I believe happened with this card: the designers intended this card to reflect a "Secret Horde," with an effect akin to a Methuselah negotiating resources from his ancient social group. But the artist had "Hoard" in mind, and made the artwork accordingly to show a secret stash of things, or understood that "horde" was meant but wasn't sure how to depict this to match the effect on the card, and therefore designed a secret stash of anthropological looking things like skulls, texts, and ancient chemicals. To further confuse things, the keyword "investment" was added to Camarilla edition.

So today, we have a card with artwork showing a stash of stuff with the word "investment." So it certainly looks like hoard was meant. But I really think "Horde" was meant because a hoard is already secret, so "Secret Hoard" would be redundant ("secret secret fund"). But who knows?

Messages.Author: Ke.
Messages.Body:
> Kraus wrote:
> But WHY does the Nosferatu royalty breed deck (already a not-so-powerful deck) have an absolute offender of a card, namely Secret Horde? Shouldn't those two copies be another copy of Warsaw Station, and a Direct Intervention instead?
>
Sure, some of the decks could be improved. Most are user submitted and providing they meet below the criteria below then they're approved:

Decks should be close to 60 cards in size (less to print) Decks should focus on one or two mechanics only Cards should be fairly simple and not contain walls of text Include deck description and rough overview on how to play
A lot of decks submitted aren't even legal — some with 100+ cards, invalid grouping, 20 crypt cards etc... the list goes on. I was torn about having it curated or not initially; however over time and seeing what's been submitted I think it was the right call.

One thing I would like to expand on in Amaranth is the social side of things. For example there's an experimental feature that allows multiple people to work on the same deck/s — that is pretty cool. I think public feedback on the quick start decks would also be useful.

Amaranth now has over 1000 registered users (whoot!) so it would be great to build on that further.

Amaranth Deck Building Tool :  VTES NZ :  VTES ANZ Facebook
